holidays.name: National Alfred Hitchcock Day
holidays.description: A day for movie buffs to binge classic thrillers like Psycho, Vertigo, and Rear Window. You can also spot his cameo in each film and practice your best dramatic shower-scene screech, though maybe not in the shower.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It matches neither the filmmaker's birthday (August 13) nor the date of his death (April 29).
holidays.funFact: Hitchcock made cameo appearances in most of his films. He often did it early in the movie so viewers could stop hunting for him and follow the plot.

holidays.name: International Fanny Pack Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble belt bag, worn at the waist or across the chest. It has been a symbol of hands-free convenience and either peak dad fashion or peak hipster cool, depending on who you ask. Strap one on and celebrate.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates an accessory that has gone in and out of fashion across generations and continents.
holidays.funFact: In the UK and much of the world, the same accessory is called a bum bag. The name changes, but the hands-free convenience does not.

holidays.name: National Genealogy Day
holidays.description: A day for tracing your roots. Dig through old photos, quiz your relatives, and find out who your ancestors were, including the scandalous ones.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It falls at the end of winter, when it is a good time to stay in and dig through family history.
holidays.funFact: Genealogy is among the most popular hobbies in the world. Many people who start with a simple family tree end up with a decades-long research project.
